policy.policy: All forced defenses; all one-move-loss escape points when at most nine; otherwise nine-PV engine screening with a 220-score / six-ply mate band, preserving prior viable choices. Terminal examples when no escape exists. A non-forced white four is dropped before any of this when its forced block ends the game, gives Black a VCF he lacked, or leaves every White reply losing to VCF.
policy.tempoFourPolicy: Omit a nonessential white four only when the identical full recorded continuation remains legal and wins with and without its forced white-four/black-block exchange. Preserve forced defenses. Replace all-redundant menus with the shortest verified suffix, including singleton and chained exchanges; audit grafted menus against that recorded strategy.
policy.oppositeFourThreePolicy: When Black has any next-move standing four-three or open four and no immediate five, cover every attack with a direct White block. Retain existing choices; add quiet blocks of uncovered attacks, each followed by a fixed finish at another attack point: a standing four-three, or an open four played out to five. At most nine choices, prioritizing occupation of attack points and coverage of every side before additional nearby blocks; when nine are not enough, a choice whose attacks another choice covers makes way.
